notes: Matching copies show in the command palette's own results as you type, so you can paste one without opening the history first (Stackbar 0.20.0). Turn it off in Settings.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.clipboard.description:
Everything you copy, searchable, pinnable and one keystroke from being pasted
back. ⌘⇧V opens it from anywhere: type to filter, ↑↓ and Return (or ⌘1 to ⌘9)
to paste into the app you were in, ⌥Return to paste as plain text, ⌘P to pin
and ⌥⌫ to delete. Formatted text keeps its formatting, and images are kept by
the host and pasted back.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: the clipboard. Passwords are skipped: the host never hands out items an app marks as concealed or transient, and copies from password managers (or any app you add) are ignored. Copies that look like secrets (API keys and tokens, JSON web tokens, private keys, card numbers, six-digit codes) are shown masked, kept out of agent tools, and dropped after 15 minutes unless you pin them.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, window, settings. Hotkey ⌘⇧V.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: how many items to keep, the order, pasting directly or only copying, showing matching copies in the palette's results, keeping images, plain text by default, how long to keep secrets (not at all, 5 minutes to an hour, or like any copy), apps and text patterns to ignore, and pausing the history.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Clipboard History, Paste Last Copy as Plain Text, Pause Clipboard History, Ignore Next Copy.

facts.label: Agent tools
facts.text: `recent_clips`, `search_clips` and `copy_clip`.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
First release: hold Right ⌘ and press a letter to switch apps, and pin letters to the apps you use most.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.app-switche.description:
Switch apps without ⌘Tab. Hold **Right ⌘** and press an app's first letter:
S for Safari, X for Xcode. If several apps share a letter, pressing it again
moves to the next one. If only one does and it's already in front, pressing
it again hides it (or shows its next window, if you prefer). Letters with no
app pass through, so Right ⌘ C still copies.

To pin a letter, bring an app to the front and press **Right ⌘ ⌥** plus the
letter. A pinned letter opens the app even when it isn't running. Hold Right
⌘ on its own for a moment to see the whole letter map.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: `.keyLayer` and `.apps`. Stackbar listens to the keyboard and switches apps for the plugin, so Stackbar asks for Accessibility access the first time. Stackbar 0.16.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, settings.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: the key you hold (Right ⌘, ⌥, ⌃ or ⇧), what pressing the letter of the app in front does, the letter map, automatic letters, and opening pinned apps.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Pin a Letter to an App, Clear App Switcher Pins.

facts.label: Agent tools
facts.text: `letters`.

facts.label: Not covered
facts.text: jumping between Spaces, a window grid, and searching for apps by name (Spotlight does that). While an app has Secure Input on, such as in a password field, macOS blocks every keyboard listener. The panel tells you which app has it on.

notes: First release: the palette's app search, now a plugin.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.application.description:
Your apps and System Settings panes in the command palette, as Spotlight and
Raycast have them. Type a few letters ("saf", "vsc", "wi-fi") and the app
comes first in the results; Return opens it, ⌘K copies its path or bundle id.
The ones you open most rank higher. Search Applications lists them all.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: the list of installed apps and opening them (`.apps`), and opening System Settings panes by their link. Stackbar 0.20.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel (your most opened apps).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Applications, which also feeds the palette's results.

facts.label: Looks in
facts.text: /Applications (one folder deep), ~/Applications and the system's own apps, plus every pane System Settings lists.

notes: First release: the palette's calculator, now a plugin.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.calculator.description:
Sums and unit conversions answered right in the command palette. Type
`12*(3+4)`, `2^10`, `15% * 80`, `sqrt(2)`, `3h in min`, `72 f to c` or
`5 km in mi`, and the answer comes first in the results. Return copies it and
⌘Return pastes it. Plain numbers and words get no answer, so it never crowds a
normal search. The panel keeps your last ten answers.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: nothing. Stackbar 0.20.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Calculate.

facts.label: Units
facts.text: length, mass, time, data, volume and temperature. No currencies.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.docker.description:
Your containers in the menu bar. The number is how many are running; the
panel lists them grouped by Compose project, with Start, Stop, Restart,
Logs, Open (for a published port), Copy ID and Remove.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: to run `docker`, from Docker Desktop, OrbStack, Colima or Rancher Desktop. No network, files or secrets of its own.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, settings.

facts.label: How it checks
facts.text: `docker ps --all` every 15 seconds while something runs, every minute otherwise.

facts.label: When something goes wrong
facts.text: a container that crashes (exits with an error on its own), turns unhealthy or keeps restarting sends a notification, turns the menu bar red with a count, and gets a banner in the panel until it is started again or removed. Stops from the panel don't count.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: show stopped containers, group by Compose project, the trouble notification (on by default), and Remove Stopped Containers (`docker container prune`; images and volumes are left alone).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Docker Containers, Docker Logs (the last 200 lines of one container), Remove Stopped Docker Containers.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `containers` lists every container with its image and state.

notes: First release: every emoji in a searchable grid in the palette.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.emoji.description:
An emoji picker in the command palette. Search Emoji opens a grid of every
emoji, grouped as Unicode groups them, with the ones you use most at the top.
Type to narrow it ("party", "thumbs up", "flag japan"), move with the arrow
keys, and press Return to paste the emoji where you were typing. ⌘K copies it
instead. The panel keeps your frequent ones a click from the clipboard.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: the clipboard, to paste (your clipboard is put back afterwards). Stackbar 0.20.0 or later, which draws grids in the palette.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Emoji. Give it a hotkey in Settings › Commands.

facts.label: Data
facts.text: Unicode's Emoji 15.1 list and English names, without skin-tone variants. Nothing leaves your Mac.

notes: First release: the palette's file search, now a plugin.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.file-search.description:
Files and folders by name in the command palette, from Spotlight's index.
Type three letters or more and the best matches show under Files in the
results, most recently used first, each with its Finder icon. Return opens
one; ⌘K shows it in Finder or copies its path. Search Files lists up to 20.
Apps, anything inside an app or bundle, hidden files and Library internals
are left out.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: finding files by name with Spotlight (names and paths in your home folder only, nothing is read from inside them), and opening what you pick. Stackbar 0.20.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel (what you opened lately).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Files, which also feeds the palette's results.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.homebrew.description:
What Homebrew can upgrade, in the menu bar. The number is how many formulae
and casks are outdated; the panel lists them with Upgrade on each row and
Upgrade All at the bottom.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: to run `brew` (Stackbar finds it in `/opt/homebrew/bin` or `/usr/local/bin` and asks you to approve that path once). No network, files or secrets of its own.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, settings.

facts.label: How it checks
facts.text: hourly and on wake it runs `brew outdated --json=v2`, which reads what Homebrew already knows. When that list is more than 6 hours old it runs `brew update` first (from the second check after launch, so the list shows right away), so the count doesn't go stale; the panel says how old the list is. Update Homebrew fetches it now.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: show casks, hide pinned formulae, include casks that update themselves (`--greedy`), fetch the latest formulae every 6 hours (on by default), and a notification when new updates appear.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Upgrade All Homebrew Packages, Update Homebrew, Outdated Homebrew Packages.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `outdated` lists what can be upgraded.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.jira.description:
Your Jira Cloud issues in the menu bar and the palette. The number is how
many assigned issues are in progress; the panel lists them, in progress
first.


Jira Server and Data Center aren't supported: only Atlassian's cloud sites.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: `*.atlassian.net` and the secret `JIRA_API_TOKEN`, an API token from id.atlassian.com (Security > API tokens). Your site and email are set in Settings.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, settings.

facts.label: On each issue
facts.text: Open, Copy Link, Copy Key, Copy Branch Name (`ABC-123-short-summary`, which Jira's development panel links).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: My Jira Issues, Search Jira (text, or a key like `ABC-123`), Create Jira Issue (project, type, summary, description).

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: site, email, the JQL behind the menu bar and panel (open issues assigned to you by default), and the default project for new issues.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `assigned` lists your open issues.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.linear.description:
Your Linear issues in the menu bar and the palette. The number is how many
assigned issues are in progress; the panel groups everything assigned to you
by state, ordered by priority.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: `api.linear.app` and the secret `LINEAR_API_KEY`, a personal API key from Linear (Settings > Security & access).

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, settings.

facts.label: On each issue
facts.text: Open, Copy Branch Name (Linear's own, so the branch links back to the issue), Copy Link, Copy ID.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: My Linear Issues, Search Linear Issues (by title), Create Linear Issue (team, title, description, priority, assign to me).

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: what the menu-bar number counts, and the default team for new issues.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `assigned` lists your open issues with their branch names.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.litellm.description:
Tokens, spend and budget from your own [LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai)
proxy, with charts. The panel has:

- **Tiles** for today, the last 7 days and the last 30 days, with tokens,
  spend, active days and the daily average.
- **Budget**: spend against your key's budget and when it resets.
- **Activity**: six months of daily tokens as a heatmap.
- **Trend**: a week as bars, or a month or six months as an area chart, in
  tokens or spend.
- **Models**: the top five models over 30 days, with each one's share.
- **Today's requests**: the success rate, how much input came from the
  cache, and what caching saved.

The menu bar shows today's spend, today's tokens or the share of the budget
used (you choose in Settings), and it turns orange at 75% of the budget and
red at 90%.


Ported from vee-plugins' `litellm-cost`.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: two secrets. `LITELLM_PROXY_URL` is your proxy's base URL, like `https://litellm.example.com`, and the plugin can reach that host and no other. `LITELLM_API_KEY` is a LiteLLM key. Both are kept in the Keychain. Nothing is contacted until you enter the URL.

facts.label: Calls
facts.text: `/user/info` and `/user/daily/activity`, every two minutes for the last 30 days and every six hours for the six months before that.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, window, widget, settings.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: what the menu bar shows, and notifications at 90% and 100% of the budget.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `usage_summary`.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.music.description:
What's playing in Music or Spotify, in the menu bar. Click it to play or
pause; right-click for the panel with the track, Previous, Next and volume.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: to run `osascript`, the only way to talk to Music and Spotify. The install sheet warns that osascript can run any program; this plugin only sends the fixed scripts in its source. macOS asks once whether Stackbar may control Music or Spotify.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, widget, settings.

facts.label: How it checks
facts.text: every 5 seconds, and only players that are already running; it never opens one.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: which player to follow (whichever is playing, Music or Spotify) and what the menu bar shows (title and artist, title, or just the icon).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Play or Pause Music, Next Track, Previous Track, Copy Current Track.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `now_playing` describes the current track.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.pomodoro.description:
A focus timer in the Stackbar look: red for focus, teal for breaks. Pick Focus or Break, a preset (25, 50 or
90 minutes of focus; 5, 10 or 15 of break), and press play. The countdown and
the ring around it move on their own, the menu bar shows the time
left (dimmed behind a pause sign while paused), and a chime and a
notification mark the end. Today's finished sessions
and focused minutes sit under the timer.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: nothing. No network, files or secrets.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, widget, settings.

facts.label: In the panel
facts.text: the tag chip cycles through your tags; skip ends the session without counting it; Auto starts the next session on its own; the note turns the sound on or off; reset clears the timer.

facts.label: No lost sessions
facts.text: once a session is a minute in, a mode, preset, skip or reset tap asks first, with a banner to confirm or keep going.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Start or Pause Pomodoro, Start a Focus Session (optional minutes and tag), Take a Break (optional minutes), Skip and Reset. Run them from the palette, give them a hotkey, or call them from a Shortcut or a `stackbar://commands/io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.pomodoro/<command>` link.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: custom focus and break lengths, auto-start, the sound, and your tags.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `status` returns the mode, the time left and today's focus.

facts.label: Requires
facts.text: Stackbar 0.14.0 or later.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.ports.description:
Which process is listening on which TCP port, and a way to stop it. The
command you'll use most is **Kill Port** from the palette: type `3000` and
whatever holds it is asked to stop.


Processes owned by another user, like system services, can't be stopped
from here.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: to run `lsof` and `kill` (both come with macOS). No network, files or secrets.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel, settings. No menu-bar item.

facts.label: In the panel
facts.text: every listening port with its process and pid, marked local (127.0.0.1 or ::1 only) or open (all interfaces). Each row can open `http://localhost:<port>`, stop the process (SIGTERM), force quit it (SIGKILL) or copy its pid.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: hide ports below 1024 (or 3000).

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Kill Port (port, and TERM or KILL), Listening Ports.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `listening` lists ports with their processes.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.system-moni.description:
CPU and memory in the menu bar, with the processes using the most a click
away.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: to run `top`, `vm_stat`, `df` and `kill` (all come with macOS). No network, files or secrets.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, widget, settings.

facts.label: How it measures
facts.text: every 10 seconds, `top` takes two one-second samples (the second is the accurate one), `vm_stat` gives memory the way Activity Monitor counts it (app memory, wired and compressed, not the file cache), and `df` the disk.

facts.label: In the panel
facts.text: a CPU chart for the last five minutes, load averages, memory and disk bars, and the top eight processes, each with Copy PID and Quit Process.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: what the menu bar shows (CPU and memory, CPU, or memory) and whether processes are sorted by CPU or memory.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `usage` returns CPU, memory, disk and the busiest processes.

notes: Tasks now live in Apple Reminders, so they're on your iPhone, iPad and Watch too. Your existing tasks move over the first time. Prefer them on this Mac only? Choose that in Settings.
Reminders lists are your categories: filter the panel by list, or type #listname in a task.
Break a task into small, medium and big steps; its row shows the next small step to tick.
Paste several lines to add several tasks at once.
An optional nudge, only on days you haven't ticked anything off yet.
Calmer: nothing is overdue any more; earlier tasks wait under "Still on your list".
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.todo.description:
A calm to-do list for the menu bar, in a warm orange. Type a task the way you
would say it and the when comes out of the words: “Call the dentist tomorrow
at 2pm” becomes *Call the dentist*, due tomorrow at 2:00 PM. Today's tasks
(and any left over from earlier) sit on top, then tomorrow, then what is
coming up, then someday. A small ring in the header fills as today's tasks get
done.

Tasks live in **Apple Reminders**, so they're on your iPhone, iPad and Watch
too, and Siri can add to them. Big tasks break into small steps.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: Reminders (`.reminders`). Stackbar asks macOS once. Say no, or pick “This Mac only” in Settings, and tasks stay on this Mac instead.

facts.label: Lists
facts.text: your Reminders lists are Todo's categories. Pick one at the top of the panel to see just that list, type `#groceries` in a task to file it in Groceries, or move a task from its editor. New tasks go to the list on screen, or your default list. (Apple doesn't let apps use Reminders' sections, tags or subtasks, so those stay in the Reminders app.)

facts.label: Steps
facts.text: open a task and choose *Break into steps*, then type a step and press Return for each one. Tap S, M or B to size a step. The task's row shows its next step (small ones first) with a circle to tick it, and how many are done; ticking the last one finishes the task. Type `Plan the offsite: book a venue; send invites` to add a task with its steps in one go. In Reminders, steps are a ☐ checklist at the end of the notes, so you see them on your phone too.

facts.label: Brain dump
facts.text: paste or type several lines and each becomes a task.

facts.label: Sync
facts.text: changes go to Reminders as you make them, and changes from your other devices come in as Reminders gets them. Only the fields you changed are written, so an edit here never undoes one made on your phone. It all works offline; macOS syncs Reminders when you're back online.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, widget, settings.

facts.label: Typing dates
facts.text: today, tonight, tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, friday, this friday, next friday (the Friday of next week), this weekend, next week, next month, in 3 days, in 2 hours, in half an hour, Nov 5, 5 November, the 12th, 2027-03-12. Times: 2pm, 2:30pm, 14:30, at 9, noon, this morning, this afternoon, this evening. Repeats: every day, every weekday, every monday, every week, every month, daily, weekly, monthly. A `!` on its own marks the task important. Words in "double quotes" are kept as they are.

facts.label: In the panel
facts.text: tick the circle to finish a task; tick a done one to bring it back. Click a task to open it in place: rename it (a date in the new text reschedules it), move it to Today, Tomorrow, the weekend, next week or Someday, set a repeat, star it or delete it. Every add, tick, move and delete shows a banner with Undo. The eye button shows what you have done.

facts.label: Repeats
facts.text: ticking off a repeating task records it as done and moves it to its next day.

facts.label: Alerts
facts.text: in Reminders, a task with a time gets a Reminders alert, on every device, with Done and Snooze. On this Mac only, Todo sends one notification when it is due; one the Mac slept through by more than half a day is let go quietly.

facts.label: One nudge
facts.text: optionally, one notification at a time you choose, only on days you haven't ticked anything off, naming a small step to start with.

facts.label: No guilt
facts.text: nothing is ever “overdue” or red. Tasks from earlier days wait under *Still on your list*.

facts.label: Menu bar
facts.text: a quiet count of what is due today, or the next task, the count of everything open, or just the icon. It never turns red.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Add a Todo, Mark a Todo Done, Snooze a Todo (to a time you type, or an hour or a day later) and Today's Todos (a list to tick off from the palette). Run them from the palette, give them a hotkey, or call them from a Shortcut or a `stackbar://commands/io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.todo/add?task=…` link.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: where tasks live, what the menu bar shows, alerts and their sound, the nudge, a morning summary of the day at 7, 8, 9 or 10 AM, and how long done tasks are kept.

facts.label: Agent tools
facts.text: `tasks` lists open tasks with their dates; `add` adds one from plain words.

facts.label: Requires
facts.text: Stackbar 0.18.0 or later.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.translate.description:
Translates the text you selected. Run **Translate Selection** from the
palette, or give it a hotkey in Settings > Commands. When an app doesn't
share its selection, it uses what you last copied.


  In place, you can paste the result over the selection (your clipboard
  comes back afterwards) or copy it, and the result says which engine did it.
  Text that is already in your target language is translated into your second
  language instead, so one command goes both ways.

facts.label: Engines
facts.text: - **Automatic**, the default, translates in place with no setup. It uses Apple's translation on your Mac when that language pair is downloaded (System Settings > General > Language & Region > Translation Languages), so nothing leaves the Mac. Otherwise it sends the text to Google Translate's keyless endpoint, the one Google's own browser extension uses. Google doesn't document that endpoint, so it may change or be rate limited. - **DeepL:** translates in place with your DeepL API key; the free plan covers 500,000 characters a month. - **Browser:** opens translate.google.com with the text filled in.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: the selection (`.context`), the clipboard (as a fallback, and to paste), `translate.googleapis.com`, `api-free.deepl.com` and `api.deepl.com`, and the secret `DEEPL_API_KEY`, which is asked for only when you choose DeepL.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel, settings. No menu-bar item.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: the engine, the language to translate into and the second language, and DeepL's formality.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Translate Selection, Translate Selection in Google Translate.

notes: First release: snap the front window from the palette or a hotkey.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.window-layo.description:
Snaps the front window to a half, a quarter, a third, the middle or the whole
screen, or sends it to the next display. Every layout is a command, so you can
type "left half" in the palette or give any layout a hotkey in Settings ›
Commands. Restore puts the window back where it was before its last snap.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: `.windows`: the host moves windows through Accessibility, so Stackbar asks for Accessibility access the first time. Stackbar 0.20.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel (a button for every layout), settings.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: the gap left around snapped windows.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Left Half, Right Half, Top Half, Bottom Half, the four quarters, First / Center / Last Third, First / Last Two Thirds, Maximize, Almost Maximize, Center, Next Display and Restore.

facts.label: Not covered
facts.text: windows in full screen or on other Spaces. To remember a whole arrangement per monitor setup, use Workspaces.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
First release: save your window layout for each monitor setup and get it back when you plug in or undock.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.workspaces.description:
Remembers where your windows go for each monitor setup and puts them back.
Arrange things the way you like at the desk, type "Desk" and press Return;
do the same on the laptop alone. When you plug in or unplug a display (or
wake the Mac on a different set of displays), the starred layout for that
setup comes back by itself, and apps that weren't running are opened.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: `.windows`: the host lists and moves windows through Accessibility, so Stackbar asks for Accessibility access the first time. Stackbar 0.15.0 or later.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, settings.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: bring back the starred layout when displays change, open apps that aren't running.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Save Window Layout, Restore Window Layout, and one Restore command per layout, so each layout can have its own hotkey or alias.

facts.label: Agent tools
facts.text: `layouts`, `save_layout` and `restore_layout`.

facts.label: Not covered
facts.text: windows in full screen and on other Spaces, browser tabs, snapping and tiling (macOS does that).

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.plugins.world-clock.description:
The time in the cities you work with. The menu bar shows one city; the panel
lists them all with the offset from you, whether it is already tomorrow or
still yesterday there, and whether it is working hours (weekdays, 9 to 18 by
default).

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: nothing. No network, files or secrets.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, widget, settings.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: the cities (type a time zone like `Asia/Tokyo`, or a city name like `Tokyo`), which one the menu bar shows, 12- or 24-hour time, and your working hours.

facts.label: In the panel
facts.text: tap a city to show it in the menu bar. The time-travel slider moves every clock up to 12 hours either way in half-hour steps, so you can see what time it is everywhere when it's 3pm here; Now puts it back. The menu bar and widget always show the real time.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: World Clock lists your cities with their times; each row can be copied or shown in the menu bar.

facts.label: Agent tool
facts.text: `times` returns the time in every city.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Switching tabs is quicker: a refresh now fetches pull requests, issues and the inbox side by side instead of one after another, and a click no longer waits as long behind it.
A new **Updated within** setting shows only pull requests and issues changed in the last week, two weeks, month or three months, and fetches only those pull requests.

io.navbytes.stackbar.pr-cockpit.description:
Your pull requests and the ones waiting on your review, with CI, review state
and merge conflicts, in the menu bar; the issues assigned to you; and your
repositories and new issues from the palette. It tells you when someone asks
for your review, when an issue is assigned to you, and when one of your own
pull requests is approved, gets changes requested, or fails its checks.

The separate GitHub plugin is now part of PR Cockpit. If you had it, you can
uninstall it: its repositories, assigned issues and Create GitHub Issue are
all here, with the same `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: network access to `api.github.com` only, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret kept in the Keychain. A fine-grained token with read access to pull requests, issues and metadata covers everything except creating issues, which needs write access to issues.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel (To review, Mine, Issues and an optional Inbox), window, widget, settings.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: include team review requests, include drafts, how recently a pull request or issue must have changed to show (any age, or the last week to three months), notifications, repositories (include archived, copy clone URLs as SSH or HTTPS, reload), repositories to hide, and the inbox view.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Pull Requests, Review Queue, Open Next Review, Search GitHub Repositories (yours first, recently opened on top, then GitHub search; each row opens the repository, its pull requests, issues or Actions, copies the clone URL, or starts a new issue), My GitHub Issues, Create GitHub Issue, Refresh Pull Requests.

facts.label: Agent tools
facts.text: `review_queue`, `my_pull_requests` and `my_issues`.

notes: **Fallbacks:** a search quicklink can be offered under the palette's results for anything you type ("Use “…” with Google"). Google, DuckDuckGo, Kagi, Perplexity, Ask Claude and Wikipedia start as fallbacks; switch any quicklink in its form. Needs Stackbar 0.20.0.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.quicklinks.description:
Links and folders you open by name from the palette, Spotlight, a hotkey or a
link, with placeholders filled in as you go. Each quicklink becomes a command
of its own. Links use Raycast's template syntax:
`https://github.com/search?q={argument name="query"}` asks for a query,
`{clipboard}` and `{selection}` take what you copied or selected, and
`{date format="yyyy-MM-dd"}` gives today's date.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: opening links and folders (in the app each quicklink names), the clipboard, and what you had selected, for `{clipboard}` and `{selection}`.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel, settings.

facts.label: Getting started
facts.text: an empty panel offers eight everyday links in one click, and Browse Quicklink Library has 40 ready-made searches, sites and folders (Search, Developer, Productivity, Mac) to add one by one or all at once.

facts.label: Order
facts.text: the ones you open most, and most lately, come first in the list and the launcher.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: your quicklinks, the library, and importing a Raycast export.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Quicklinks, Create Quicklink, Browse Quicklink Library, Import Quicklinks, Export Quicklinks (a file Raycast reads too), plus one command per quicklink.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.snippets.description:
Text you paste by name, with placeholders filled in. Each snippet becomes a
command of its own that pastes into the app you were in, then puts your
clipboard back. Snippets use Raycast's template syntax: `{clipboard}`,
`{selection}`, `{date format="d MMM"}`, `{argument name="who"}` asks first,
`{cursor}` leaves the caret there, and `{snippet name="Signature"}` pulls in
another snippet.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: the clipboard (to paste), what you had selected for `{selection}`, and 16 MB of storage for the snippets.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: panel, settings. Hotkey ⌃⌥S opens Search Snippets.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: your snippets, and importing a Raycast export.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Search Snippets, Create Snippet, Import Snippets, Export Snippets (a file Raycast reads too), plus one command per snippet.

facts.label: Not yet
facts.text: keywords are kept but not expanded as you type, because that needs a system-wide keyboard monitor.

notes: Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.stay-awake.description:
Keeps your Mac awake for a while, until a time, while an app runs, on a
weekday schedule, or until you say stop. It lets go when the battery runs low,
and the host releases the sleep assertion if the plugin ever stops or
crashes, so it can't leave the Mac awake by accident.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: power management (the sleep assertion), through the host.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, widget, settings.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: keep the display on, the battery floor, pausing in Low Power Mode, a notification when it ends, what a click does, a weekday schedule, and staying awake while plugged in, on an external display, on a VPN or while downloading, and whether the menu bar shows the time left as digits or a ring.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Toggle Stay Awake, Keep Awake For… (`90m`, `2h` or `17:30`) and Allow Sleep. Give them a hotkey or an alias in Stackbar's Settings, or run them from Spotlight, Shortcuts or a `stackbar://` link.

facts.label: Agent tools
facts.text: `awake_status`, `keep_awake` and `allow_sleep`.

notes: Its store screenshots no longer show a meeting under both Today and Tomorrow.
Store screenshots now show it in use, with sample data, instead of its first-run screen.
Its own icon and colour in the Store and in Settings.

io.navbytes.stackbar.up-next.description:
Your next meeting in the menu bar, with a countdown and one-click join. It
finds the video link in the location, URL or notes (Zoom, Meet, Teams, Webex
and a dozen more), reminds you a few minutes before, and can open the call for
you when it starts.

facts.label: Needs
facts.text: your calendars in Calendar.app, through the host, which asks for access once. No network.

facts.label: Surfaces
facts.text: menu bar, panel, window, widget, settings. Hotkey ⌃⌥J joins.

facts.label: Settings
facts.text: calendars to hide, all-day and declined events, only meetings with a link or with other people, the reminder lead time, auto-join, a full-screen alert, how the title shows in the menu bar, and opening calls in their apps.

facts.label: Commands
facts.text: Join Next Meeting, Copy Next Meeting Link and Today's Meetings. Give them a hotkey or an alias in Stackbar's Settings, or run them from Spotlight, Shortcuts or a `stackbar://` link.

facts.label: Agent tools
facts.text: `next_meeting`, `agenda` and `join_next`.
